Every design decision in this plan traces back to one or more of them.\n8\t\n9\t1. **Deterministic order.** Given the same queue state, every worker computes the same bead ordering. There is no randomness in selection. Ties are broken by creation time.\n10\t\n11\t2. **Explicit outcome paths.** Every possible result of every operation has a named handler. If an outcome can happen, it has a handler. If it doesn't have a handler, it cannot happen. The type system enforces exhaustiveness.\n12\t\n13\t3. **Platform and model agnostic.** NEEDLE wraps any headless CLI that accepts a prompt and exits. It runs on any POSIX system. It does not depend on any specific AI provider, model, or API.\n14\t\n15\t4. **Observable by default.** Every state transition, claim attempt, dispatch, and outcome emits structured telemetry. A silent worker is a broken worker. Telemetry is structured from origin (JSONL) and exportable as OpenTelemetry (OTLP) so any compliant backend — Tempo, Jaeger, Grafana, Honeycomb, Datadog, FABRIC — can consume NEEDLE's signals without a custom adapter.\n16\t\n17\t5. **Self-healing.** Workers detect and recover from stuck states, stale claims, crashed peers, and corrupted databases without human intervention. Recovery paths are explicit, not heuristic.\n18\t\n19\t6. **Separation of concerns.** The orchestrator does not execute work. The agent does not manage state. The bead store does not enforce workflow. Each component has one job.\n20\t\n21\t---\n22\t\n23\t## Architecture Overview\n24\t\n25\tNEEDLE is composed of five layers:\n26\t\n27\t```\n28\t┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n29\t│                        CLI Layer                              │\n30\t│  needle run | stop | list | Claiming, locking, heartbeats, peer awareness                │\n37\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n38\t│                    Agent Layer                                 │\n39\t│  Adapter interface, dispatch, result capture                  │\n40\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n41\t│                   Foundation Layer                             │\n42\t│  Telemetry, configuration, bead store interface, self-healing │\n43\t└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n44\t```\n45\t\n46\t### Component |\n70\t|-------------|-----|--------|\n71\t| Exhaustive pattern matching | Every outcome must be handled; compiler enforces it | Principle 2, bead-lifecycle-bugs.md |\n72\t| Real module system | 45K single-file bash was unmaintainable | bash-at-scale-problems.md |\n73\t| Structured error types | Silent failures caused cascading bugs | claim-race-conditions.md |\n74\t| Native JSON support | Fragile jq parsing corrupted state | worker-starvation-lessons.md |\n75\t| Proper concurrency primitives | flock/trap/PID files were inadequate | concurrency-approaches-compared.md |\n76\t| Single binary distribution | NEEDLE must be trivially installable | Principle 3 |\n77\t| Cross-platform | Linux, macOS at minimum | Principle 3 |\n78\t| Static analysis | Catch undefined functions, unused variables at compile time | bundler-build-integrity.md |\n79\t\n80\t**Recommended: Rust.** Exhaustive `match`, `Result<T, E>` error handling, `serde_json`, `tokio` for async, single binary via static linking, cross-compilation. The beads ecosystem already has Rust precedent (beads_rust, beads-polis).\n81\t\n82\t**Acceptable alternative: Go.** Simpler learning curve, good concurrency, single binary. Lacks exhaustive matching (requires discipline instead of compiler enforcement).\n83\t\n84\t**Not acceptable: Bash, Python, Node.** Bash failed at scale (documented). Python/Node require runtime dependencies, violating single-binary distribution.\n85\t\n86\t---\n87\t\n88\t## Key Decisions from Research\n89\t\n90\tThese decisions are informed by the 14 research files in `docs/research/`:\n91\t\n92\t| Decision | Chosen Approach | Alternative Considered | Why |\n93\t|----------|----------------|----------------------|-----|\n94\t| Bead store interface | Abstract trait over `br` CLI | Direct SQLite access | Platform agnostic; works with future bead backends |\n95\t| Claim atomicity | `br update --claim` + workspace flock | Central coordinator (Perles) | No SPOF; works with decentralized workers |\n96\t| Heartbeat model | File-based heartbeat with TTL (from beads-polis) | Shared memory | Survives worker crashes; observable by peers |\n97\t| Validation gates | Pluggable gate system (inspired by bg-gate) | Hardcoded checks | Different workspaces need different validation |\n98\t| Work decomposition | Built-in mitosis with child-aware dedup | External only (spec2beads) | Mitosis is valid when the split criteria are semantic (multi-task detection) and dedup checks the parent's existing children |\n99\t| Self-modification | Allowed with release channel promotion (testing → stable → fleet hot-reload) | Prohibited entirely | v1 failures came from untested changes deploying directly to the fleet. Canary testing with defined inputs/outputs prevents this. |\n100\t| Workspace discovery | Explicit configuration | Filesystem scanning | Explore strand's unbounded find caused 35+ load |\n101\t| Alert system | Verify-then-alert with rate limiting | Alert-on-empty | 100% false positive rate from naive alerting |\n102\t\n103\t## Key Decisions from Operational Learnings\n104\t\n105\tThese decisions are informed by the 9 notes files in `docs/notes/`:\n106\t\n107\t| Learning | Design Response |\n108\t|----------|----------------|\n109\t| Mitosis explosion (5,741 duplicate beads) | Mitosis checks parent's existing children before creating new ones. Duplicate splits are structurally impossible. Split criteria are semantic (multi-task detection), not numeric. |\n110\t| 100% false positive starvation alerts | Three-state model: no beads exist / all claimed / invisible. Verify independently before alerting. |\n111\t| Bundler shipped undefined functions | Compiled language eliminates this class entirely. |\n112\t| Agent-owned closure most reliable | NEEDLE does not close beads. Agent receives `br close <id>` instruction in prompt. |\n113\t| stdout/stderr corruption | Telemetry is a structured system, never interleaved with agent output. |\n114\t| Workers modifying their own orchestrator | Self-modification allowed via release channels. New builds must pass canary tests in isolation before promotion to `:stable`. Fleet hot-reloads from `:stable`, never from `:testing`. |\n115\t| ~20 worker practical limit (EX44) | Fleet sizing is bounded by three runtime factors: provider inference throughput, available CPU, and available RAM. NEEDLE monitors these and warns when saturated. Staggered launch is default. |\n116\t| Bead granularity affects success rate | Document guidelines but don't enforce — this is a bead authoring concern, not orchestration. |\n117\t\n118\t---\n119\t\n120\t# State Machine\n121\t\n122\tThe worker loop is a finite state machine. Every state has defined entry conditions, actions, and exit transitions. There are no implicit states or fallthrough paths.\n123\t\n124\t## Worker States\n125\t\n126\t```\n127\t                    ┌──────────┐\n128\t                    │  BOOTING │\n129\t                    └────┬─────┘\n130\t                         │ config loaded, health check passed\n131\t                         ▼\n132\t                    ┌──────────┐\n133\t              ┌────►│
